entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Alan I, King of Brittany, played a crucial role in shaping the medieval landscape of Western Europe. Born around 860 CE, he rose to power as the Count of Vannes and Duke of Brittany, eventually becoming the only King of Brittany to hold the title by imperial grant. His reign was marked by significant territorial gains, strategic alliances, and cultural exchanges with neighboring kingdoms and the Catholic Church. Alan I's legacy continued through his descendants, who would go on to play important roles in the history of Brittany and France. Notably, the Treaty of Chartres, signed in 876 CE, established the boundaries of Brittany and solidified Alan I's territorial claims. His impact on the region's politics, economy, and culture has been lasting, making him a significant figure in regional history.
